title: Green Pesto Pasta Salad with Cherry Tomatoes and Rocket
changes_from_base: The oil-and-vinegar dressing, mozzarella, peppers and olives are replaced by a basil, spinach and toasted pine nut pesto made creamy with mayonnaise, with cherry tomatoes and rocket.
summary: This vibrant variant follows the same cook-and-toss method as our classic Italian pasta salad, but swaps the oil-and-vinegar dressing, mozzarella, peppers and olives for a basil, spinach and toasted pine nut pesto made silky with a little mayonnaise, finished with cherry tomatoes and peppery rocket.
equipment: whisk or jam jar with a lid

ingredients.item: fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (1%)
ingredients.note: about 6.75 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, for the pasta
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast the Pine Nuts
steps.text: Tip the pine nuts into the dry frying pan and toast over medium-low heat for 4-5 minutes, shaking the pan often, until they turn an even pale gold. Keep the heat gentle and your eye on the pan, since pine nuts have a high oil content and can burn within seconds once they start to colour. Set 2 tablespoons aside for scattering later and leave the rest to cool.

steps.title: Cook and Cool the Pasta
steps.text: Once the nuts are toasting, bring 4 litres of water to the boil in the large pot, stir in the salt, and cook the pasta for 1 minute longer than the packet time; the extra minute makes sure it's fully tender before it cools and firms up again. Scoop out 120 ml of the starchy cooking water and set it aside, then drain the pasta, toss it with the 1 tablespoon of oil so the pieces don't stick together, and spread it on the tray to cool for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Blend the Pesto
steps.text: In the food processor, blitz the cooled toasted pine nuts with the garlic until finely chopped, then add the basil, spinach and lemon juice and pulse a few times. With the motor running, pour in the olive oil in a steady stream until the mixture turns a bright, loose green. Pulse in the grated hard cheese, mayonnaise, salt and pepper; the spinach keeps the colour vivid, while the mayonnaise gives the pesto a creamy body that clings to the pasta even once it's cold.

steps.title: Toss Pasta with Pesto
steps.text: Back in the large bowl, toss the cooled pasta with the pesto until every piece is coated, then loosen it with 2-4 tablespoons of the reserved cooking water, a little at a time, until it turns glossy rather than clumped. The starch left in that water helps the sauce spread evenly without needing any extra oil.

steps.title: Add Tomatoes and Rocket
steps.text: Last of all, fold the halved cherry tomatoes and rocket through the pasta just before serving, so the rocket keeps its peppery crunch instead of wilting. Scatter the reserved toasted pine nuts over the top for extra bite and colour. A quick taste here lets you check whether it needs more salt or lemon.

tips: Toast the pine nuts in a completely dry pan over gentle heat and watch them closely — they go from golden to burnt in moments.
Check your hard cheese label for an animal-rennet-free version if that matters to you; vegetarian hard cheeses work just as well in the pesto.
Save a little pasta water before draining — it's the easiest way to loosen the pesto without diluting its flavour.
Add the rocket just before serving rather than stirring it in early, as it wilts quickly once dressed.
Common mistake: running the processor too long so the pesto heats up and dulls in colour — pulse rather than blend continuously.
storage: Best eaten within a few hours of making. If needed, keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 day, adding the rocket only when you're ready to serve so it stays crisp. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
